__doc__: sim-collision-dt-render-lead-floor-v1: the integration-lane hand-off for the cold-collect ladder (twin-robot-in-store-boot-v1). coldwin30 (cold full cycle, PR 304+307+308) tripped collect preplace at sim 129 s with `CONTROLLER_INVARIANT_TRIP phase=preplace now=129.000 collision_dt=-0.5333(band [-0.5,1.5])`: the mirrored collision stamp (nvblox ESDF integration time, on the Isaac render clock) LED the controller node clock `now` by 0.533 s -- a FRESHER collision world, not stale -- but the band FLOOR had been hand-set to -0.5 via RESTOCK_FRESH_RENDER_LEAD_S=0.5, 0.033 s too tight. The lane then bumped the env to 0.7 by hand for coldwin31 and the trip cleared with zero over-band samples. This PR makes that floor a DERIVED, logged default so the env bump is unnecessary and the widening is recorded in every run dir.
_what_changed: twin.restock.physics_step.collision_band_floor(render_lead_base, dt) = (render_lead_base + COLLISION_RELAY_LEAD_S[0.5] ESDF-incorporation window) * freshness_scale(dt). At the DEFAULT step and the default 0.2 s delivery lead this is 0.7 s -- exactly the hand value. The TransferController derives self.render_lead from it (controller.py); the positive (stale) CEILING (max_age) and the trip name are UNCHANGED -- only the future-lead floor gains headroom (a future lead is strictly MORE current data -- safe). Generalises PR 288's step-aware rule to the default step: the ESDF-window term contributes 0.5 s even at 1/60, where the pure base*freshness_scale scaling was a no-op.

_action_for_the_integration_lane.DROP: RESTOCK_FRESH_RENDER_LEAD_S -- remove it from the mission-runtime env for twin-robot-in-store-boot-v1. The floor now derives to 0.7 at the default step with no env; leaving the env set still works (it raises the delivery term) but is no longer needed and risks over-widening (e.g. 0.5 -> floor 1.0).
_action_for_the_integration_lane.KEEP: RESTOCK_SENSOR_MAX_AGE_S=1.5 -- the stale (positive) ceiling is out of scope for this lane and is unchanged.
RESTOCK_PHYSICS_DT behaviour -- run_mobile_restock still exports it from config['physics_dt']; the derived floor scales with it automatically (1/36 -> floor 0.7*5/3 = 1.167).

_expected_next_run: coldwin32 (or the next cold full cycle) reaches the SAME collect verdict as coldwin31 (no collision_dt floor trip) WITHOUT the RESTOCK_FRESH_RENDER_LEAD_S override. The remaining collect blocker is coldwin31's CARTON_TILT 2.07 deg at the PR 307 south-dock place geometry (a DIFFERENT lane: the 2.0 deg bound + 0.15 s grace are captain-fixed; do not loosen them here).
_what_to_grep: grep -n 'COLLISION_FRESHNESS_BAND' host-stack.log   # MUST be present: records the derived floor=-0.7000 ceiling=1.5000 band in force (this run's widening is never silent)
grep -nE 'collision_dt=.*\(band' host-stack.log <mission-console>.log   # MUST be ABSENT (no future-lead floor trip at collect)
grep -nE 'arm command heartbeat lost' <mission-console>.log   # MUST be ABSENT (the floor trip's downstream death)
_cpu_proof: scripts/twin/tests/test_collision_dt_render_lead_floor.py -- replays coldwin30's recorded collision_dt trace (the exact -0.317 boot / -0.5333 preplace-trip values from host-stack.log + the steady ~-0.55 per-tick proxy): every sample is FRESH under the derived -0.7 floor, the -0.5333 sample is below the legacy -0.5 floor (fix is load-bearing), and a synthetic truly-stale trace STILL trips at the unchanged ceiling. Plus the derivation unit (collision_band_floor) and the logged-band summary. Also updated: test_physics_step_collision_band.py controller-band assertions and test_restock_manipulation.py fm423 future-lead tests.
_data: firstmate/data/sim-collision-dt-render-lead-floor-v1/: report.md, collision_dt_distribution.json (coldwin30: all 8219 collect ticks below the -0.5 floor, 0 below -0.7; coldwin31 same, passed), collision_dt_histogram.png (before/after), coldwin30_collision_dt_trace.json.
_out_of_scope: Anything outside the freshness band. The ~0.55 s two-clock lead itself (why the Isaac render clock leads the host packet clock by a steady 0.55 s on a COLD live_pose run, vs the documented 0.05 s cold offset) is tolerated, not removed -- a follow-up could tighten the relay instead of widening the floor.
